items.title: Spatial metabolomics reveals brassinosteroid-mediated compartmentalization of saikosaponin biosynthesis in Bupleurum chinense DC. under abiotic stress
items.summary: Although the biosynthesis of active ingredients in medicinal plants is co-regulated by diverse environmental stimuli, the endocrine mechanism by which brassinosteroids (BRs) coordinate physiological resilience with the in situ spatial distribution of saikosaponins in Bupleurum chinense DC. under combined drought and salinity remains largely elusive. We hypothesized that exogenous brassinosteroids (BRs) application alleviates oxidative impairment provoked by single and combined osmotic/ionic stresses while orchestrating the tissue-level topological routing of saikosaponin biosynthesis. items.title: Current developments on taxonomy, agronomy, bioactivity and in vitro micropropagation of two Malaysian ginger varieties: Zingiber officinale Rosc cv. Bentong and Zingiber officinale Rosc cv. Rubrum
items.summary: Zingiber officinale Rosc., or ginger, is a widely cultivated tropical herb species belonging to the family Zingiberaceae. Ginger is renowned for its medicinal and culinary uses. In Malaysia, two prominent ginger varieties, Z. officinale Rosc. cv. Bentong (Bentong ginger) and Z. officinale Rosc. cv. Rubrum (red ginger), are highly valued for their distinctive properties and significant economic importance. Bentong ginger, recognised by its geographical indication associated with the Bentong district of Pahang, is characterised by elongated leafy stems up to 90 cm in height arising from large, horn-shaped rhizomes with a strong aroma and high phenolic contents. items.title: Antimicrobial Activity and Antioxidant Potential of Peppermint Essential Oil (Mentha piperita L.) Against Selected Pathogenic Microorganisms Extracted via Hydrodistillation with Electromagnetic Field (EMF) Pre-treatment
items.source: Baghdad Journal of Biochemistry and Applied Biological Sciences
items.summary: Background: Antimicrobial resistance is increasing concerns, and there is interest in natural antimicrobials including plant essential oils, which are potentially induced to be of higher quality by non-thermal methods such as low-frequency electromagnetic field pre-treatment. The aim of this objective is to extract and characterise Mentha piperita essential oil, pre-treating the seeds with Electrosonics wave (EMF) in order to test its antimicrobial and antioxidant activity. items.title: Engineered strains as living factories: efficient biosynthesis and modification of natural products via synthetic biology and one-pot chemical tandem reactions
items.summary: Natural products are a crucial source for drug discovery, but their traditional development is limited by resource availability, efficiency, chemical complexity, and the difficulty of rapidly diversifying biologically active scaffolds. This review addresses the central question of how biosynthetic precision and chemical diversification can be coupled when conventional metabolic engineering alone cannot fully overcome low titers, enzyme promiscuity limits, intermediate toxicity, and scale-up heterogeneity.
